text:
hana-cs: Heads-up: AcmePay reports missing usage in Console for the last ~6 hours, shows 0 tokens between 10:00-16:00 UTC. Ticket #12345. Screenshot link: https://redwood.app/attachments/12345.png

mike-support: Ack. I'm seeing the same gap for tenant 'acmepay' on the usage dashboard. Going to query raw events quickly.

mike-support: ```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM events.usage WHERE tenant_id='acmepay' AND ts >= '2026-03-06T10:00:00Z' AND ts < '2026-03-06T16:00:00Z';
-- returns 0
```

lisa-dataeng: Checking ingestion pipeline — quick glance shows usage-aggregator consumer group has high lag.

ops-bot: ALERT: kafka consumer group usage-aggregator lag > 5M messages (topic: usage-events) at 2026-03-08 17:12:34 UTC :rotating_light: 

devon-sre: Can someone run consumer describe for the usage-aggregator group? Need offsets.

jordan-ml: I ran a quick check from my laptop, here's the output I got: 
```bash
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group usage-aggregator
TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
usage-events    0          1245000         1299000         54000
usage-events    1          1243000         1298000         55000
usage-events    2          1244000         1298500         54500
```

lisa-dataeng: Looks like consumer is falling behind; downstream writer is the bottleneck. I'm checking Airflow 'hourly-rollups' DAG for failures.

mike-support: Airflow web UI shows last successful run for hourly-rollups at 2026-03-07 23:00 UTC; subsequent runs failed with DB timeout errors.

mike-support: ```text
[2026-03-08 16:58:12] ERROR airflow.models.taskinstance TaskInstance failed
Task airflow_task 'hourly_rollup' failed: OperationalError: timeout while writing to usage_rollups (pool exhausted)
```

devon-sre: Checking k8s — I see pod `usage-writer-0` OOMKilled a few times earlier and restarted, now in CrashLoopBackOff for ~20m.

ops-bot: k8s event: Namespace=prod Pod=usage-writer-0 Reason=OOMKilled Count=3 at 2026-03-08T16:55:02Z

lisa-dataeng: Proposed mitigation: scale usage-writer to 3 replicas and temporarily bump DB connection pool to 50. Also increase consumer parallelism to 6. Approve?

mike-support: Approve. Do it carefully during low traffic window. Also prepare backfill plan and notify the customer about a partial outage for their usage graph.

jordan-ml: I'll prepare a dry-run backfill for the affected window. Proposed command: 
```bash
python tools/backfill_usage.py --tenant acmepay --start '2026-03-06T10:00:00Z' --end '2026-03-06T16:00:00Z' --dry-run
```

lisa-dataeng: Running dry-run now. If results look good I'll launch the real backfill after writer pods stabilize. ETA ~45m for stabilization + 30m for backfill.

hana-cs: I'll update the customer: "We're investigating ingestion lag caused by a consumer/backpressure issue; engineers are scaling writers and planning a backfill. Expect updates in ~1h." Ticket updated and escalated to P1.

devon-sre: Scaling to 3 replicas and bumping DB pool to 50 now. Watching logs.

analytics-bot: Backfill queued: job_id=bf-9876 tenant=acmepay window=2026-03-06T10:00:00Z..2026-03-06T16:00:00Z estimated_events=12134 status=queued

devon-sre: Writer pods now stable. Consumer lag dropping: 55000 -> 2100 within 12m.

mike-support: Confirming dashboard: data points are starting to populate for AcmePay around 14:00-15:00 UTC range; still catching up.

lisa-dataeng: Backfill job started: job_id=bf-9876 running. I'll monitor for duplicates and skews.

analytics-bot: job_id=bf-9876 status=running progress=65% processed=7900/12134 errors=0

hana-cs: Notifying customer: "We started the backfill and the console will reflect missing usage within ~30 minutes as data replays. Apologies for the disruption"

mike-support: :white_check_mark: Backfill completed job_id=bf-9876 processed=12134. Reindex done.

lisa-dataeng: Post-backfill checks: sample query matches historical counts, no duplicate events detected, hourly-rollups DAG caught up.

hana-cs: Customer confirmed they see the missing hours in Console. I'll close the incident after 2h stable monitoring.

mike-support: Thanks all — document root cause as: consumer lag due to usage-writer OOM -> DB pool exhaustion -> airflow rollups failed -> dashboard gap. Action items: 1) increase writer memory + liveness probe tweak, 2) add autoscaler for writer, 3) alert on consumer lag > 50k for 10m.

lisa-dataeng: I'll file a follow-up RFC for autoscaling and runbook updates.

mike-support: Closing escalation in ticketing system, marking as mitigated.
